card.title: Workload Risk: off-hours activity elevated
card.summary: 45% of 120 commit/review events occurred off-hours (20 on weekends, 34 at night, UTC) across 4 contributors.
card.suggestedAction: Review workload distribution across the team and encourage healthier working-hours boundaries.
card.limitation: Only GitHub commit/review timestamps were analyzed. Off-hours are computed in UTC without timezone normalization.

aiAnalysis.summary: Off-hours contributions have risen notably this window, concentrated in late-night commits. This can indicate schedule pressure worth reviewing.
limitations: Only GitHub commit/review timestamps were analyzed. Off-hours are computed in UTC without timezone normalization.

items.title: Elevated off-hours activity
items.detail: 45% of commit/review activity happened outside business hours (UTC), across 4 contributors.

items.title: Rebalance review and delivery load
items.detail: Check whether deadlines or review bottlenecks are pushing work into evenings and weekends, and redistribute where possible.

contributorInsights.note: Contributed 21 commits and 9 reviews. 18 of 30 (60%) landed off-hours — 11 at night and 7 on weekends (UTC). Carries the largest share of off-hours coding load this window.
contributorInsights.suggestion: Protect their evenings by moving non-urgent work into business hours and sharing feature ownership.

contributorInsights.note: Contributed 8 commits and 14 reviews. 15 of 22 (68%) landed off-hours — 9 at night and 6 on weekends (UTC). Acts as a primary reviewer, often unblocking peers late.
contributorInsights.suggestion: Add a backup reviewer so review turnaround does not depend on their off-hours availability.

contributorInsights.note: Contributed 14 commits and 5 reviews. 12 of 19 (63%) landed off-hours — 8 at night and 4 on weekends (UTC).
contributorInsights.suggestion: Check whether task deadlines are forcing evening work and adjust scope for the next cycle.

contributorInsights.note: Contributed 10 commits and 4 reviews. 9 of 14 (64%) landed off-hours — 6 at night and 3 on weekends (UTC).
contributorInsights.suggestion: Encourage protecting weekends and flag if the current sprint load is unsustainable.
